reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only supports the feasibility of powder-metallurgy processing of refractory HEAs and mentions improved ductility via SPS; it does not provide any data on Ag incorporation, wetting behavior, network formation, thermal conductivity enhancement, or mechanical compatibility of an Ag interlayer. The key premises regarding the Ag intervention are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Refractory HEAs can be processed by powder metallurgy and SPS to achieve densification and improved ductility
A thin Ag interlayer can be introduced during transient liquid phase sintering
Ag melts and wets HEA particles at 1100–1200 °C, forming a continuous network upon cooling
An interconnected Ag network provides enhanced electron/phonon transport, raising thermal conductivity by ~30%
The Ag network does not form deleterious weak interfaces or brittle intermetallics that compromise structural integrity
